thread:
maya: heads up — CI started cleaning up SAST/DAST artifacts after 24h and we lost evidence for at least 2 blocker PRs. noticed during triage this morning.
aj: yikes. which pipeline?
maya: the new unified-scan job. retention lifecycle added in the job config last week, defaulted to 24h. it deletes s3://redwood-ci-scans/artifacts/<run-id>.
ron: @maya do we have an incident? can we recover the artifacts?
maya: not a formal incident yet but triage was blocked. tried to restore via s3 versioning — bucket didn't have versioning enabled.
sam: scan-bot reported findings at 07:12 and 07:15, then ci-bot ran cleanup at 07:30. scan-bot searchable logs only show summary, not raw traces or vulnerable file diffs.
scan-bot: automated: alert -> high-confidence SNYK-like match on dependency chain in service-invoicing. evidence id: scan-2026-07-16-8142. (this is bot message)
aj: we should prevent deletion for runs flagged as "blocker". retention policy should be: blockers => 30d, high => 7d, low => 1d. also add audit log entry for any delete action.
maya: agreed. quick mitigation: disable cleanup job until we patch the pipeline. who can flip that? @sec-oncall?
sec-oncall: I can flip the toggle in the CI config, but we need a rollback plan since storage costs could spike. proposal: disable cleanup for 48h, backfill policy that sets longer retention for runs with severity>=high, and enable a scan-only retention label.
ron: also need RBAC change: only security-admin, sec-oncall, and infra-deploy role can delete artifacts. current CI service-account has delete privileges. we should scope it to put/get, not delete.
sam: +1. Current IAM policy: 
```
{
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:PutObject","s3:GetObject","s3:DeleteObject"],"Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::redwood-ci-scans/*"}
  ]
}
```
We should change DeleteObject -> Deny unless request has tag "ci:allow-delete=true" or principal in security-admins.
aj: we can implement attribute-based access control via AWS STS session tags from the console and from the sec-oncall role. also add KMS-enforced audit: encrypt artifacts with a key that requires an allow_delete key policy binding. deletions should be logged to CloudTrail with KMS:Decrypt events.
maya: question: if we encrypt with a KMS key that only security-admins can use for rewrap/delete, will that block normal reads by CI? we need CI to still fetch files to upload to external triage tools.
aj: CI should be given kms:Decrypt for artifacts it needs to read, but not kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion or kms:DisableKey. Deletion of an object still happens at S3 layer; we protect by IAM deny on DeleteObject. KMS controls key operations, not object deletes. but we can augment delete flow to require a separate KMS-wrapped ticket check — e.g., require delete requests to include a signed header from the key-holding service.
ron: simpler: enforce IAM deny on DeleteObject for the service-account; any manual deletion goes through a small service owned by security that signs a short-lived token after review. token is presented by a CI job that calls the delete service. that gives an audit trail.
sam: agree. we should also retain the raw patch/diff and stack traces in an encrypted evidence bucket and add lifecycle to move to Glacier after 90d for cost.
maya: to unblock triage now, can someone run a quick grep across runner ephemeral workspaces? maybe some artifacts are still on the runners that did the scans. run ids: 2026-07-16-8142 and 2026-07-16-8143.
aj: i'll spin up a retrieval job to query runners and ask infra to snapshot any live ones. if nothing, we escalate to the repo owners to re-run scans with the same commit hash (but that delays triage).
sec-oncall: action items I will take now: 1) disable cleanup toggle (48h) 2) add chatops confirmation block for any future cleanup toggle changes 3) open a PR to change IAM to remove s3:DeleteObject from CI service account 4) draft deletion flow service owned by security.
maya: I'll notify the triage owners and mark the affected PRs as "evidence missing - recovery in progress". also add an eval test to the premerge policy to tag runs with severity labels stored as artifact metadata.
ron: addendum — we need audit log retention for delete attempts: CloudTrail + an internal readonly log shipping to our SIEM for 1y. cannot rely on S3 access logs only.
sam: small config snippet for a lifecycle rule suggestion: 
```
Action: AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload after 7 days
Transition non-blocker artifacts to GLACIER after 90 days
Expire artifacts with tag "temp=true" after 1 day
Keep artifacts with tag "severity:blocker" for 30 days
```

aj: +1. i'll author the PR for IAM + lifecycle + the delete-service spec. sound like we have consensus? :thumbsup:
maya: consensus. thanks everyone. let's follow up in the PR thread and update the incident board if we need a ticket.
ci-bot: automated: cleanup job disabled by sec-oncall at 2026-07-16T08:05:27Z.
maya: confirmed triage unblocked for one PR — scan-bot still needs re-run for the other. I'll coordinate re-run with the author. :raised_hands:
